# The classical theory: a selection rule from $\Theta$ {#sec-classical}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- See how the antilinear symmetry $\Theta$ acts on solutions and on Hirota data.
- Prove that $\Theta$-invariant solutions have real energy, momentum and higher charges.
- Recognise the solutions excluded by this rule: complex-energy and singular solutions.
- Understand the missing-charge problem.
:::

The solitons of @sec-classical-solitons are complex fields, yet their energies are real. The literature established this case by case, and also found complex solutions with complex or negative energies. This chapter shows that a single symmetry decides which solutions have real conserved charges. It is the classical counterpart of the Krein-space structure of the quantum theory (Part VII).

## $\Theta$ on solutions {#sec-theta-classical}

In @sec-real-imaginary we saw that $\overline{V_{\rm imag}(\vec\phi)}=V_{\rm imag}(-\vec\phi)$. On complex fields, define

$$
\Theta:\vec\phi\mapsto-\bar{\vec\phi} .
$$

Conjugating the field equation (-@eq-toda-eom) shows that $\Theta$ maps solutions to solutions. On the Hirota form (-@eq-hirota-ansatz), $-\bar{\vec\phi}=\frac i\beta\sum_j\frac{2\vec\alpha_j}{\alpha_j^2}\ln\bar\tau_j$, so $\Theta$ acts by $\tau_j\mapsto\bar\tau_j$. For the $a_n^{(1)}$ solutions (-@eq-n-soliton), $\overline{\omega^{ja}}=\omega^{j(h-a)}$ and $\overline{A_{ab}(\theta)}=A_{h-a,h-b}(\bar\theta)$, so on the data of each constituent soliton

$$
\Theta:(a,\theta,\xi)\mapsto(\bar a,\bar\theta,\bar\xi),\qquad\bar a=h-a .
$$ {#eq-theta-data}

A real field is $\Theta$-invariant only if it is odd, $\vec\phi=-\vec\phi$, so the interesting invariant solutions are complex. The sine-Gordon kink, for which $\bar a=a$, is mapped to a solution with the opposite topological charge and conjugate $\xi$.

## Reality of energy and momentum {#sec-reality-energy-momentum}

::: {#prp-hirota-energy}
**[Established; reformulated]** For a Hirota solution, the energy and momentum densities are total derivatives [@olive1993a; @olive1993b]. They integrate to

$$
E=\sum_iM_{a_i}\cosh\theta_i,\qquad P=\sum_iM_{a_i}\sinh\theta_i,
$$

where $(a_i,\theta_i)$ are the species and (possibly complex) rapidities of the constituent solitons [@tw1999, eq. 4.6]. The masses $M_a$ are real and positive. The same holds for all higher conserved charges [@freeman1995].

:::

On Hirota data, $\Theta$ acts as $\tau_j\mapsto\bar\tau_j$. That is, $(a,\theta,p)\mapsto(\bar a,\bar\theta,\bar p)$, where $\bar a$ is the conjugate species ($\omega^{ja}\mapsto\omega^{-ja}$). Consequently:

- **Selection rule.** If the asymptotic data $\{(a_i,\theta_i)\}$ are $\Theta$-invariant, meaning the rapidities are real or occur in conjugate pairs with conjugate species, then $E$, $P$ and all conserved charges are real. Solitons and breathers are of this kind.
- **Complex energies.** The complex-energy solutions of Khastgir and Sasaki have asymptotic data that are not $\Theta$-invariant. They are not in the physical sector, for the same reason that complex eigenvalues of a $\Theta$-symmetric operator are not $\Theta$-invariant states (@sec-antilinear).

This closes gap H6 of @sec-critique, apart from the question of singularities. The restriction to "good" solutions, previously ad hoc, is the classical shadow of @thm-krein-transfer.


**Examples.**

- A single soliton with real rapidity $\theta$ is covered by the rule, and $E=M_a\cosh\theta$ is real. ($\Theta$ maps it to a soliton of the conjugate species, which has the same mass.)
- A breather (@sec-breathers) has asymptotic data $\{(a,\theta_0+iu),(\bar a,\theta_0-iu)\}$, which $\Theta$ maps to itself. Its energy $2M_a\cosh\theta_0\cos u$ is real, although each constituent has complex rapidity.
- A single soliton with complex rapidity $\theta_0+iu$ alone has $E=M_a(\cosh\theta_0\cos u+i\sinh\theta_0\sin u)$, complex for $\theta_0u\neq0$. Its data are not $\Theta$-invariant, and it is excluded.

## Singular solutions {#sec-singular-solutions}

Zeros of $\tau_j$ in the real $(x,t)$ plane are isolated points: one complex condition, two real conditions. There the energy density has double poles with zero residue, so integrated charges are unaffected, and the Hirota data continue analytically through the singularity.

The genuinely problematic phenomenon is different. In theories with non-self-conjugate species, soliton–breather scattering produces complex time delays and can carry regular data into singular regions [@tw1999]. This is the classical image of a quantum sector in which $\Theta$ is broken (@sec-sector-status). It is not a failure of the formalism.

## The missing-charge problem {#sec-missing-charges}

The quantum solitons of species $a$ form a multiplet of $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$. For $a_n^{(1)}$ this is the $a$-th fundamental representation, whose $\binom ha$ weights are the possible topological charges. The classical single solitons of @sec-topological-charges carry only $h/\gcd(a,h)$ of them [@mcghee1994]. The species-1 solitons of every $a_n^{(1)}$ carry all their charges, but already for the species-2 soliton of $a_3^{(1)}$ four of the six weights are missing.

There are three possible responses.

- **The classical theory is incomplete.** Other classical solutions, not single Hirota solitons, carry the missing charges. Multi-soliton bound states at complex rapidities are candidates.
- **Semiclassics is incomplete.** The missing states appear only quantum mechanically, through saddles of the path integral that are not real-time solutions.
- **Both.** Static complex saddles are not enough. @sec-which-saddles-contribute shows that for $a_3^{(1)}$ no static saddle of the right energy carries the missing weights, and conjectures (@cnj-missing-charge) that complexified two-soliton bound states at the fusing angle carry them.

The problem is gap H11 of @sec-critique, and it is open.

## Exercises {#sec-classical-exercises}

::: {#exr-theta-solutions}
Show that $\vec\phi\mapsto-\bar{\vec\phi}$ maps solutions of the imaginary-coupling field equation to solutions. Show that it is not a symmetry of the real-coupling field equation, and find the antilinear map that is.
:::

::: {#exr-theta-interaction}
Show that $\overline{A_{ab}(\theta)}=A_{h-a,h-b}(\bar\theta)$ for (-@eq-interaction-coefficient), and deduce (-@eq-theta-data) for multi-soliton solutions.
:::

::: {#exr-breather-real}
Show that the asymptotic data of a breather are $\Theta$-invariant. If moreover $\xi_2=\bar\xi_1$, show that $\bar\tau_j=\tau_j$ and that the field is purely imaginary. For sine-Gordon, show that the real breather (-@eq-sg-breather) instead has $\xi_2=\bar\xi_1+i\pi$.
:::

::: {#exr-singular-points}
Show that a zero of $\tau_j$ in the real $(x,t)$ plane is generically an isolated point, and that near it the energy density has a double pole with zero residue, so that integrated charges are unaffected.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-classical-notes}

Reality of soliton energies was shown by Olive, Turok and Underwood [-@olive1993a; -@olive1993b] and Zhu and Caldi [@zhu1995], and of all conserved charges by Freeman [-@freeman1995]. Complex-energy and negative-energy solutions are in Khastgir and Sasaki [-@khastgir1996], and the complex time delays and singular final states of $a_2^{(1)}$ in Takács and Watts [-@tw1999]. The missing charges were found by McGhee [-@mcghee1994]. The formulation as a selection rule from $\Theta$ is new here.
